questions.text: New taxes on wealth or property, such as a capital gains tax, wealth tax or land value tax, should be introduced to help fund public services.

lab: A simple, targeted 28% tax on profit from selling investment property after 1 July 2027.
https://www.labour.org.nz/our-policies/
grn: Introduce a super-rich tax of 2.5% on net wealth over $10 million so that multimillionaires pay their fair share.
tpm: Implement a net wealth tax on the wealthiest individuals to address extreme inequality and fund essential public services.
top: a Land Value Tax to lower house prices
nat: National is committing to no new taxes if re-elected on November 7.
https://www.national.org.nz/policies/no-new-taxes
act: Balance the Government’s books without new taxes and return to surplus faster.

questions.text: The company tax rate should be cut, at least for small and medium businesses.

nzf: lowering the company tax rate for SMEs to 20% for companies with turnover under $30million, from its current 28% tax rate.
tpm: Return the company tax from 28% back to 33%.

questions.text: KiwiSaver contributions should be compulsory.

nat: From 1 July 2028, National will make contributions to KiwiSaver (or an equivalent scheme) compulsory for all workers.
https://www.national.org.nz/policies/kiwisaver
nzf: compulsory KiwiSaver enrolment for the wider workforce and increasing employee and employer contributions to 8% initially and eventually to 10%.
lab: Employer contributions become compulsory from 1 July 2028, including when an employee reduces or pauses their own contributions
https://www.labour.org.nz/strengthening-kiwisaver
Compulsory for employers only; employees can still reduce or pause.
act: Other parties want to force your money into KiwiSaver, then tax you. ACT says it should be your choice

questions.text: The minimum wage should be raised to the living wage.

tpm: Immediately raise the minimum wage to the living wage ($28.95 per hour)
grn: Work towards matching the minimum wage to the living wage.
A goal to work towards, not an immediate change.
act: Freeze the adult minimum wage for three years

questions.text: People on benefits should face stricter work obligations, with sanctions or reduced payments if they don't meet them.

nat: From 1 April 2028, jobseekers who have received Jobseeker for two of the previous three years will move to a lower rate of payment
https://www.national.org.nz/policies/walfare
act: if you can work, you should be taking real steps toward work, and taxpayer support should go to the essentials it was intended to fund.
grn: Increase benefits to liveable rates, individualise benefit entitlements and abolish benefit sanctions.
tpm: Remove financial penalties, sanctions, and work-test obligations.

questions.text: Government spending should shrink as a share of the economy.

nat: Keep taxes low by right-sizing government, with core Crown expenditure as a share of the economy declining towards 30 per cent of GDP
https://www.national.org.nz/policies/responsibility-rules
act: New Zealand needs a smaller, more efficient government
lab: keep core Crown expenditure and revenue at around 33% of GDP in the medium term
https://www.labour.org.nz/our-policies/
Holds spending steady rather than cutting it.
grn: Public services should be treated as investments in our shared future, not costs to cut.

questions.text: Councils should be legally capped in how much they can raise rates each year.

nat: requiring councils to keep annual rates increases within a target range of 2-4%
https://www.national.org.nz/policies/rates-capping

questions.text: The government should step in directly to break up the supermarket duopoly.

nzf: break up Foodstuffs into two nationwide cooperatives based on brand
lab: Our first step to break up the supermarkets will be to free small grocers from anti-competitive restraints that keep prices high.
https://www.labour.org.nz/fairer-grocery-prices
grn: Create KiwiMart, a publicly owned supermarket chain with a single mandate - keep prices down.
nat: if the Commerce Commission confirms that a separation stacks up, we will pursue it. If it doesn’t, we won’t.
https://www.national.org.nz/policies/grocery-competition
Would split New World and PAK’nSAVE, subject to the Commerce Commission.
top: the power to break up duopolies and other uncompetitive markets via the High Court.
Gives the Commerce Commission the power; break-up decided case by case.
tpm: Break corporate control by supporting Māori-owned supermarkets and protecting local kai sellers.
act: Rather than joining the race to the bottom where we attack successful businesses, ACT’s policy is to make it easier for new businesses to come here, compete, and expand.

questions.text: The big power companies should be split into separate electricity generators and retailers.

nzf: We will split the big power companies up into generators and retailers.
tpm: We will ensure regulators have the power to intervene more structurally if regulation does not deliver fair prices
Structural intervention only if regulation fails.
act: Oppose forced break-ups of the major companies that generate and sell electricity.
top: No. Structural separation is a lengthy and costly solution, and doesn't address the core issues in the electricity sector.

questions.text: The Reserve Bank should aim for full employment as well as low inflation.

lab: restore the Reserve Bank's dual mandate of price stability and maximum sustainable employment
https://www.labour.org.nz/our-policies/
grn: Broadening the Reserve Bank’s focus to ensure that it supports the economy and full employment while controlling inflation.
act: Retain the Reserve Bank’s focus on controlling inflation so farmers can plan with greater confidence.

questions.text: It should be illegal for big companies to charge excessive prices for essentials.

lab: Making it illegal for big companies to overcharge for essentials.
https://www.labour.org.nz/our-policies/
tpm: A fairness framework will be mandated to regulate pricing.

questions.text: New Zealand should stay in the Paris Agreement and meet its climate commitments.

top: calls for New Zealand to recommit to our Paris Agreement obligations and protect the role of the Climate Change Commission.
grn: Ensure Aotearoa meets our Paris Agreement commitments through strong domestic action
act: Renegotiate New Zealand’s commitment under the Paris Agreement. If a fairer arrangement cannot be reached, New Zealand should be prepared to leave.
Would leave if a renegotiation fails.
nzf: New Zealand First is saying we need to get out of the Paris Accord altogether

questions.text: Farm greenhouse gas emissions (such as methane) should be priced.

grn: Introduce a price on agricultural emissions to ensure methane reduction targets are met
top: Back farmers to cut biogenic methane and nitrous oxide emissions through cap-and-trade systems, biodiversity markets and innovative technology.
act: Keep agriculture permanently out of the Emissions Trading Scheme and oppose any agricultural emissions tax or pricing scheme.

questions.text: New oil and gas exploration should be banned.

grn: Ban new fossil fuel extraction, end subsidies for fossil fuels and cancel the LNG terminal.
tpm: End new oil and gas exploration and phase out existing extraction.
act: Keep onshore and offshore petroleum exploration open where commercially viable opportunities emerge.
nzf: We will find those energy reserves, we will extract them

questions.text: It should be faster and easier to get approval for new mines.

act: Keep fast-track consenting available for eligible projects and establish clear deadlines for government decisions.
nzf: New mining zones will have clearer rules around where mining can occur, recognising regions where mining is already a key part of the economy.
nat: National will develop a new Government Policy Statement on Mining and Extraction under the Fast Track Approvals Act
https://www.national.org.nz/policies/hunters-and-anglers
top: Strengthen environmental checks on major decisions by limiting ministerial override on fast-track projects
grn: Repeal the Fast-track Approvals Act and revoke consents for fast-track approvals for new coal, gold and seabed mining projects.
tpm: Retrospectively revoke all fast-tracked mining consents.

questions.text: Seabed mining should be banned.

grn: Ban seabed mining in the coastal marine area and the exclusive economic zone

questions.text: Freshwater rules should put the health of waterways first, by restoring Te Mana o te Wai.

top: Reinstate Te Mana o te Wai to put the health of waterways first in freshwater policy
grn: Reinstate Te Mana o Te Wai to prioritise the health of freshwater in decision-making and regulation
act: Remove Te Mana o te Wai and other vague spiritual concepts from freshwater regulation, and prevent them returning under another name.

questions.text: The Waitangi Tribunal should be wound up or abolished.

nzf: immediately abolish the Waitangi Tribunal, and replace it with the Treaty of Waitangi Completion Commission.
act: Amend the Treaty of Waitangi Act so the Tribunal is automatically disestablished once all eligible historical claims have been completed
grn: Increase resourcing for the Waitangi Tribunal, providing them with the power to make binding recommendations
tpm: Amend the Treaty of Waitangi Act 1975 so that Waitangi Tribunal recommendations are binding on the Crown

questions.text: Te Tiriti o Waitangi obligations should have stronger legal force over government decisions.

tpm: The Crown must be legally accountable when it breaches its Te Tiriti obligations.
grn: Implement genuine Te Tiriti-based decision-making models across government
top: Our position is to ensure that all legislation gives proper effect to Treaty obligations.
act: Stop courts using broad Treaty interpretations to impose obligations Parliament never actually legislated.

questions.text: Public services and funding should be allocated by need only, never targeted by ethnicity.

act: If two New Zealanders have the same need, government should treat them the same.
lab: Labour will invest $21 million a year in Māori-led training that helps more whānau Māori gain skills and move into good, well-paid work
https://www.labour.org.nz/maori-trades-training
top: stable multi-year commissioning for kaupapa Māori and iwi-led providers
grn: Devolve power and redistribute resources back to tangata whenua
tpm: As Māori make up 50% of the social housing waiting list, we must ensure that half of all new social housing is allocated to whānau Māori.

questions.text: There should be a referendum on whether to keep the Māori electorate seats.

nzf: The time has come for a decision on the future of the Māori seats.
grn: Entrench the Māori electoral seats to guarantee Māori representation in Parliament

questions.text: Political donations should be capped, and only individual voters (not companies or trusts) should be allowed to donate.

top: Ban donations from companies and trusts, so only registered New Zealand voters can donate.
grn: Reform electoral funding by limiting donations to registered voters, increasing public financing of campaigns and capping a donor’s donations

questions.text: Migrants should have to live here longer before they can get welfare benefits.

nzf: New Zealand First will implement a 10-year welfare stand-down period for all visa holders
act: ACT will introduce a five-year welfare stand-down for all residence class visa holders.
nat: From 1 April 2028, the minimum residence period for main benefits will increase from two years to five years.
https://www.national.org.nz/policies/walfare

questions.text: The number of residence visas issued each year should be capped at a much lower level.

nzf: A resident visa cap of 20,000 per year.
grn: The Green Party will create fair and achievable pathways to residency for all people coming here to work

questions.text: Tougher sentences, such as three-strikes laws, are the right way to reduce crime.

act: Anyone convicted of burglary three times would receive a minimum sentence of three years in prison, with no parole, no home detention, and no early release.
nat: A vote for National is a vote for real consequences for crime.
https://www.national.org.nz/policies/tougher-sentences
top: Tough-on crime is a slogan for short-term political gain.
grn: Enable judicial discretion in sentencing, including by abolishing mandatory minimum sentences, life sentences, preventive detention, limits on sentence discounts, three strikes
tpm: Te Pāti Māori commits to the abolition of prisons by 2040

questions.text: Drug use should be treated as a health issue, with legal, regulated cannabis.

grn: treats drug use as a health issue and provides for regulated access to cannabis for personal use.
top: Regulate recreational use of cannabis to undercut organised crime and reduce youth incarceration.
tpm: Overhaul Misuse of Drugs Act so that drug use is treated as a health issue.

questions.text: Sexual consent law should require an active ‘yes’, not just the absence of a ‘no’.

nat: National will change the law to specify that consent must be actively given, meaning there must be a 'yes' rather than the absence of a 'no.'
https://www.national.org.nz/policies/consent-laws
grn: amend the definition of consent, and preclude a defence of reluctant consent to affirm that consent must be free and voluntary, and can be withdrawn at any time

questions.text: The government should make GP (doctor) visits free.

lab: Three free doctor's visits a year for everyone.
https://www.labour.org.nz/our-policies/
tpm: Invest in free primary healthcare for all whānau
grn: Work towards a publicly delivered, fully free provision of dental and primary care services

questions.text: Public transport fares should be capped low or made free.

lab: $20 a week is the most you'll pay to get around by bus or train under Labour.
https://www.labour.org.nz/our-policies/
grn: Immediately lower the fare price for bus and train trips per trip to $2 for any one trip for adults taking public transport.
tpm: Extend free public transport to everyone within 5 years.

questions.text: The law should limit how much rents can rise each year.

grn: Make rents more affordable by limiting annual rent increases to no more than 2%
tpm: Once frozen, rents will only be allowed to increase by the rate of inflation each year

questions.text: The government should build many more state houses.

lab: We will allocate $2.9 billion of capital for Kāinga Ora to build more state houses.
https://www.labour.org.nz/start-work-now
grn: Build tens of thousands of new public homes
tpm: We are committed to building more social housing in Aotearoa and to stopping the discount sale of existing state homes to private investors.
top: Direct Kāinga Ora to build the mix of housing each region actually needs

questions.text: Pay equity law should be restored so workers in female-dominated jobs can claim fairer pay.

lab: pay equity legislation restored in the first 100 days
https://www.labour.org.nz/our-policies/
grn: undoing the Government’s changes to the pay equity regime and resuming claims
tpm: Restore pay equity and ensure that Māori are paid equitably.

questions.text: Student loan debt should be cut or partly written off.

lab: A 10% cut to eligible student loan balances, with small balances under $2,000 written off completely.
https://www.labour.org.nz/our-policies/
tpm: Write off the living-cost component of all student loans.
grn: work towards fees-free tertiary education and a student debt write-off.
top: We’ll forgive student loan interest for returning Kiwis
Interest only, for Kiwis returning from overseas.

questions.text: Graduates who move overseas should face tougher measures to make them repay student loans.

nat: introduce tougher measures to recover student loan debt from people who move overseas.
https://www.national.org.nz/policies/boost-for-graduates
grn: Reduce and re-balance student loan repayments and interest rates for overseas student loan borrowers, extend the repayment holiday for overseas borrowers, and abolish border arrests for student loan repayment violations.

questions.text: Paid parental leave should be made longer.

nat: Paid parental leave entitlements will increase from 26 weeks to 30 weeks over three Budgets
https://www.national.org.nz/policies/paid-parental-leave
grn: Increase paid parental leave to 15 months for the primary caregiver

questions.text: Large data centres should have to supply their own new electricity rather than draw on existing supply.

nat: Require AI data centres to bring new, firmed power
https://www.national.org.nz/policies/electrify-nz-2
lab: Data centres will be required to secure their own renewable energy supply, pay for their own connection costs
https://www.labour.org.nz/ai-for-new-zealand
top: Require every AI data centre to fund its own clean energy, pay its full grid connection costs and publicly report its energy and water use.

questions.text: The government should set up a dedicated regulator or office to oversee AI and online safety.

lab: A new Office of AI within DPMC, and an online safety regulator
https://www.labour.org.nz/ai-for-new-zealand
grn: Regulate social media platforms to address harmful content and behaviour by introducing a Digital Duty of Care. This will require algorithmic transparency and accessible and responsive complaints systems, as well as strengthening enforcement with an independent national regulator.
top: Deliver a cross-party, national AI framework covering data rights, intellectual property and investment
A national framework rather than a new regulator.

questions.text: New Zealand should cut foreign aid outside the Pacific and spend the savings at home.

nat: We will reduce foreign aid outside the Pacific, where we will continue to support our closest neighbours and strongest interests.
https://www.national.org.nz/policies/more-medicines-and-earlier-care
grn: Restore and increase the international climate aid funding Aotearoa contributes.
Commits to more climate aid; doesn't address other aid outside the Pacific.

questions.text: New Zealand should pull back from military alliances such as Five Eyes and take a neutral foreign policy.

tpm: Legislate neutrality and prohibit participation in foreign wars unless directly threatened.
grn: Decouple military and security frameworks from the United States, including declining to participate in AUKUS and withdrawing from Five Eyes.
